scope: Complete mathematical derivation review of the two supplement texts, using their explicitly stated canonical actual-game facts. This is paper-proof review, not a claim that these counting arguments have been formalized in Lean.
method: Read both full documents; reconstruct counts, disjointness, compensation, optimization and order of limits. Independently implement exact polynomial identities plus rational Horner interval subdivision, distinct from the supplied Bernstein checker.

checks.reason: For p outside the diagonal image, diagonal MEX and row maximality give exactly one occurrence in precisely the earlier rows with d(q)>p. All diagonal owners of values at most p precede p, so the occurrence count is A(p). Distinct pre-retirement awards give distinct columns. The three cases q

Each row has q+1 distinct entries, exactly A(d(q)) of which are S labels, and one diagonal birth. Sorting an N-element subset of the diagonal image only lowers its jth order statistic; the layer-cake identity then gives G<=U minus the full excess area with coefficient one. U has the stated leading coefficient; floor and fixed-C errors are O(N).

For a live old column its inherited diagonals and prior awards are N distinct labels. The missing labels below N are exactly the S labels with victim at or below the column. For live rank i starting at 1, future history size is r_i+2-i; summing gives W+3u/2-u^2/2. Completed-owner pairs and future D awards have disjoint value ranges. Expanding C_N-T yields the displayed prefix sum plus nonnegative contributions from completed owners beyond m. This removes the entire static/birth deduction without an ordered inverse.

Each high sample N+r is distinct and lies at most N+m-1. Under the displayed range condition it cancels one area term. The remaining low area and all listed discarded terms have the claimed signs; the resulting finite inequality is m*u-alpha*W-u^2/2+L_N<=U_N.

A live column preceding the victim in its death row must already have booked the death label, so s_j<=2j-1. Envelope bounds and permanent carry prevent a retired column from booking above p_i+s_i. The lower victim bound shows every chronologically unusable column is below the later victim and disjoint from the bookers. The derived lower constraint on E(p_j) has the correct coefficients and only a fixed rank-uniform additive error.

The selected K deadline ranks have sum at least K(K+1)/2, yielding B_ret. The maximum selected rank is at least K, and distinct increasing labels give excess decrease at most lambda per backward rank. The initial boundary and discrete triangle errors are O(N); K=0 is handled separately. These are two bounds on the same excess mass and are combined by maximum, never addition.

The stated exact identity uses the right endpoint E(t) in 2E(t)Delta E(t). Its increment-square term is O(N), and the negative endpoint-square cost is retained. Only low samples p<N enter, so none is reused in high-area cancellation.

Minimization over all real z is a legitimate lower relaxation. Its two slopes have opposite signs, so the crossing is minimal. Direct substitution gives J; the low branch is strictly convex and its vertex lies between zero and the breakpoint. The upper branch is nondecreasing on v<=1. Independent rational polynomial identities verify the displayed minimum V/(2D0), and exact interval arithmetic verifies denominator positivity and the required signs.

Fixing alpha below liminf gives a finite global C. Along a liminf subsequence m/N tends to 1-beta and the endpoint excess tends to beta-alpha. The range condition follows from strict limiting inequalities. Taking N first and alpha upward second removes the endpoint cost without uniform-C estimates. Exact root brackets and strict polynomial monotonicity imply the density bound. Injectivity converts an eventual lower diagonal bound to an upper image count and then contradicts the density bound; no ordered diagonal inverse or density limit is assumed.

The floor baseline produces delta_j>=0, including a negative floor. Further ranks above the baseline cutoff add h each. On the stated parameter rectangle, the backward ramp has positive height and support strictly above .58m. Its right-endpoint integer sum dominates the triangular integral. All ranks through K precede the largest selected past deadline. Consequently early target excess is bounded by S_N-B_peak, disjoint from the ramp mass rather than an illicit sum of overlapping lower bounds.

Rank-deficit costs bound omitted ranks; Markov counts bound large source slack and target excess. The coefficients 21 and 4.1/100 follow from the displayed missing-rank constants and thresholds. Subtracting two units safely covers interval rounding. Independent exact rational interval checks establish the constants on the entire parameter rectangle.

Solving delta_i for s_i gives i+a*s_i-e_i=D*i+(a/h)*delta_i-(1+a/h)*e_i-a. Its good-source upper bound is strictly below .55m, while a good target has j-e_j>=.55m. This proves p_i+s_i<p_j. The separate bound .30m>.58m/h places each source strictly above the baseline cutoff, so every target obtains G_s additional exclusions without double counting.

Summing target slack gives X>=h*G_s*G_t. The positive-part product lower bound expands to m^2/5000-.461X-Y-.06m. Since h0*(1-.461)-1=22291/500000>0 and X>=0, rearrangement gives X+Y>=m^2/5000-.06m, hence the displayed average-plus-gain bound.

Exact rational interval tests independently verify both endpoint gaps, vertex location, breakpoint, slope and inside gain. Strict convexity below the breakpoint and monotonicity above extend the endpoint gaps outside the rectangle.

The baseline confines beta below .471. If beta>.469, fixing a between .469 and beta keeps every uniform optimization certificate applicable. The same N-first/a-second limit gives Q(beta)>=0. Independent exact coefficient expansion verifies Q=12500P-(1-beta)^3D0; rational interval monotonicity and endpoint signs isolate its unique root. Independent rational brackets prove the stated strict diagonal bound. No limsup ceiling, convergence, or algorithm is inferred.

limitations: Canonical game foundation is an explicit prerequisite; this review does not convert a paper proof into a kernel theorem.
Only liminf conclusions stated in the documents are accepted; no limit existence or faster algorithm is implied.
